events.title: Birth of Galileo Galilei
events.description: Galileo Galilei was born in Pisa, in the Duchy of Florence. He became an astronomer, physicist, and engineer who made pioneering telescopic observations of the Moon, the phases of Venus, and the moons of Jupiter.
events.significance: Often called the father of observational astronomy and modern physics, Galileo helped establish the scientific method and challenged geocentric views of the universe, leading to his famous conflict with the Catholic Church.

events.title: Sinking of the USS Maine in Havana Harbor
events.description: The American battleship USS Maine exploded and sank in Havana Harbor, Cuba, killing about 260 crew members. The ship had been sent to protect American interests during the Cuban struggle for independence from Spain.
events.significance: The incident inflamed American public opinion, fueled by sensational 'yellow journalism' and the rallying cry 'Remember the Maine!', and helped precipitate the Spanish-American War later that year.

events.title: Fall of Singapore
events.description: British forces under Lieutenant-General Arthur Percival surrendered Singapore to the Imperial Japanese Army led by General Tomoyuki Yamashita. About 80,000 British, Indian, and Australian troops became prisoners of war.
events.significance: Winston Churchill called it the worst disaster and largest capitulation in British military history. It marked the collapse of British power in Southeast Asia and the start of a brutal Japanese occupation.

events.title: Soviet Union Completes Withdrawal from Afghanistan
events.description: The last Soviet troops crossed the Friendship Bridge out of Afghanistan, ending nearly a decade of military intervention that began in December 1979.
events.significance: The withdrawal marked a major defeat for the Soviet Union, contributed to its economic and political decline, and left Afghanistan in continued civil war, setting the stage for the rise of the Taliban.

events.title: Canada Adopts the Maple Leaf Flag
events.description: The new red-and-white maple leaf flag of Canada was inaugurated at a ceremony on Parliament Hill in Ottawa, replacing the Canadian Red Ensign as the national flag.
events.significance: The flag became a lasting symbol of Canadian national identity and independence, following a lengthy national debate during Lester B. Pearson's government.
